# Lenz 0.0.22 beta

This release brings Maven and Gradle support to Lenz Code's Java editing, a calmer status bar and clearer details, and faster zip comparisons in Lenz Diff (PRs #63–#73).

- **Java projects.** A Java file outside the build (Eclipse JDT LS checks it for syntax only) now says so in the status bar and in Server Details. When a Maven profile of the project adds its folder, Lenz names that profile and F2 offers **Activate Maven Profile "…" for This File**.
- **Maven Profiles…** (F2, in a Maven project whose `pom.xml` declares profiles) sets the profiles JDT LS imports the project with. They are written to a settings file beside `providers.json` that Maven adds to your own `~/.m2/settings.xml`.
- Saving `pom.xml`, `build.gradle(.kts)`, `settings.gradle(.kts)` or `gradle.properties` re-imports the project, and open files then show the updated errors. Set `java.configuration.updateBuildConfiguration` in `providers.json` to be asked first instead.
- **Go to Definition** and Ctrl+click on `this` land on the enclosing class in Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, TypeScript, C# and C++.
- **Status bar.** It no longer blinks when you switch files: no "LSP no file", "Loading <path>…", "Line 1" or brief "indexing" flashes. It no longer shows the file's path or a sticky "LSP error" mark. Only labelled cells react to clicks: the position opens Go to Line, and **Details** (in wide enough windows) opens Status Details.
- **Status Details and Server Details** list what needs attention first, then File, Project and Language server, one labelled line each, with your home folder shown as `~`. A server's error shows its first line; the whole text goes to Logs.
- Copy buttons in dialogs and the activity log say **Copied**.
- The Markdown preview and CSV table switch is a pair of icons at the file's top-right instead of a button in the tab row.
- **Choose Language Server Runtime** lists each runtime by name with its folder, marks the one in use, and shows the highlighted one's full path. JDT LS 1.63 and later need Java 25.
- "Found no definition" notices are short and accurate: no "may still be loading" for a ready server, and the provider's limits stay in Server Details.
- Lenz Code retries starting a language server or tool that finds its file busy.
- **Lenz Diff** compares unchanged zip members without decompressing them, and pairs zips for comparison only up to 64 MiB each. Its status says when syntax highlighting stopped at its time limit.
- Archive, history, merge and syntax highlighting edge cases are handled more strictly.
- Updated the GPUI framework to v1.29.2 and the Rust dependencies.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. Lenz Diff and Lenz Code were checked on a Wayland desktop (Hyprland) and on a headless Wayland compositor. The Java changes were checked with Eclipse JDT LS 1.63.0 on a Maven project; Gradle is untested. Native macOS interaction remains unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.21](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.21...v0.0.22).
